IMPLEMENT ISSUE #936 (part of #330; #908's follow-up F1): THE REPOSITORY-ROOT BUNDLE TESTS HOLD THEIR VERDICT UNDER AN INHERITED GIT_CONFIG_COUNT. Test-only hardening. Production is right: it fails closed, by name.

You are implementing one unit on branch story-936-git-config-isolation, already checked out in this worktree off origin/main at a6c965d8b. That commit carries #908's PR #934. Where a choice is left open below, implement the option marked recommended, keep it small, and say which you took in your notes.

THE OPERATOR'S RULING: 2026-10-31, in chat, "go with recommended" (#908, https://github.com/feedback-loop-ai/brokkr/issues/908#issuecomment-6548910129): #934's landing's carried LOW F1 is a follow-up, filed as #936 (https://github.com/feedback-loop-ai/brokkr/issues/936). Decision 0071 ruling 9: a test's verdict is its own, whatever the host's environment.

THE FAILURE (#936; reproduce it first, and record the command and its output):
- A test process that inherits git's command-scope configuration through the environment fails `bundle::tests::walk_908::a_repository_root_bundle_pins_neither_git_nor_an_ignored_tree` (crates/brokkr-runtime/src/bundle/tests/walk_908.rs:151). The inherited variables:
  - `GIT_CONFIG_COUNT=1`
  - `GIT_CONFIG_KEY_0=core.excludesFile`
  - `GIT_CONFIG_VALUE_0=<a file listing roles/>`
- The ordinary repository-root fixture's charter is then refused as git-ignored: "seat 'review' names role 'roles/role.md', which stands at 'roles/role.md' — a path the bundle's file walk does not pin, because it holds a tree git ignores".
- The same test passes in a clean environment.
- `queued_launch::a_nested_folder_made_after_queueing_refuses_the_start` (crates/brokkr-runtime/tests/queued_launch.rs:382) fails the same way.
- **The cause:** crates/brokkr-runtime/tests/support/git.rs (and any in-crate equivalent the unit test uses) isolates `GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL` and `GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM` for the helper's own git calls only. Command-scope `GIT_CONFIG_*` outranks the repository's local `core.excludesFile`. It reaches `Bundle::compile`'s git children through the inherited process environment.

WHAT TO BUILD: test-only hardening that covers the process running `Bundle::compile` and every child it spawns, not just the helper's git calls.
- **Recommended:** re-execute each affected test in a cleaned environment, as `a_repository_root_bundle_pins_neither_git_nor_an_ignored_tree_under_a_hostile_global` (walk_908.rs:207, its `HOSTILE_GLOBAL` re-exec) already does. Clear `GIT_CONFIG_COUNT`, every `GIT_CONFIG_KEY_n`/`GIT_CONFIG_VALUE_n` and `GIT_CONFIG_PARAMETERS` for the child.
  - This avoids mutating the process environment in a parallel test binary. Share the re-exec through one helper rather than copying it (the clone ratchet).
- **The alternative, only if the re-exec cannot reach a case:** a guard that clears those variables and restores them on unwind, serialized against every test in that binary that reads the environment. Say why you chose it.
- **The regressions.** Each one fails before your change and passes after:
  - the walk_908 case under the planted `GIT_CONFIG_COUNT`/`KEY_0`/`VALUE_0` ignoring `roles/`;
  - `queued_launch`'s case under the same plant.
- No production change. Every existing test keeps its name and its assertions.

Removal controls (record each in the commit message, restored after the observed failure): (i) dropping the cleaning from the walk_908 re-exec fails its regression by name; (ii) the same for queued_launch.

GATES:
- cargo fmt --all -- --check
- cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features --locked -- -D warnings
- cargo test -p brokkr-runtime --lib --locked -- bundle:: (timeout 280)
- cargo test -p brokkr-runtime --test queued_launch --locked (timeout 280)
- the two regressions run once more with the plant exported in the calling shell (`GIT_CONFIG_COUNT=1`, `GIT_CONFIG_KEY_0=core.excludesFile`, `GIT_CONFIG_VALUE_0=<scratch file listing roles/>`), passing, and quoted
- typos --hidden; quality/ratchet.sh files and clones; git diff --check; every touched file under its ceiling (tests 2,000), no function over CC 15
- TMPDIR stays OUTSIDE this worktree (use /var/tmp, created in the same command if missing; if it is read-only in your box, a fresh directory under /tmp). Before reporting, `git status --short` shows no untracked file.
- Run every command in the foreground and wait for it. Never end your turn with a background job pending: this seat is non-interactive.
- A seat whose commands run through the `workspace` tool has a 300-second response limit per call. A call that outlasts it leaves its command running and blocks the calls behind it, including the write of your result file. So:
  - wrap every command in `timeout 280` there, and split a long suite by test filter;
  - if a gate still cannot finish inside the limit, report it UNVERIFIED (the controller's host coverage runs every test) rather than retrying it;
  - write your result file before any optional extra check.
- Commit when done, signed off (`git commit -s`), "tests: …" ending "(#936)", with the line "Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>" LAST, directly after the sign-off. Record each removal control in the commit message. Never push.

ASKS TO NAME (for the PR, which opens as a DRAFT only if one is new): the isolation chosen (re-exec or guard) and why; any new one.

SIZE (an estimate): +40 to +120 test lines; no production line.

KNOWN FLAKES, not this branch's:
- capability_broker tests and `machine_proof::` runs failing "MCP server box filesystem identity is not protected: admission did not complete before its startup deadline" under host load;
- brokkr-runtime engine::broker admission tests ending `Identity(Expired)` under load;
- heap_costs' one-byte compare difference under load;
- brokkr-protocol `oneshot::tests::a_produced_attempt_carries_its_result_and_checkpoints` (#932).

If verify fails on one of these alone, the implement visit reruns it on the host alone (`-- --exact`, with HOME set), quotes both results, makes no commit, and reports COMPLETE, not blocked.

CONTENTION (NEVER message the-forge-9d or any brokkr-wt-* seat):
- #753 (another lane) is in brokkr-cli tui/ and run_pages/ and brokkr-store seat_read.
- #896 (another lane) is in adapters/dsh.json, adapters/mcp/admit.rs and the dsh hands tests.
- Decision 0065 slice two (another session) is in brokkr-cli broker/rpc*, brokkr-runtime bundle/mcp.rs, engine/isolation.rs, native_controls/mcp.rs, adapters/mcp.rs and tests/capability_broker.
- Leave them all. This unit edits only brokkr-runtime's bundle tests, tests/queued_launch.rs and the test support helpers.

Every review position, panel member or chief, is READ-ONLY: it changes no tracked file and makes no commit. For a scratch, use `git worktree add` or `git archive HEAD | tar -x` into /var/tmp, never a byte copy of this worktree. It reports each finding as a test case: the environment planted, the test run, and the verdict observed against the one expected.

Decisions: 0071 rulings 2, 3, 5, 6, 8 and 9; 0083 and its #908 addendum (the bundle walk); 0063 (Linux and macOS).

# OpenSpec analyze

Judge duplication, ambiguity, underspecification, house alignment, coverage gaps, and inconsistency across proposal, deltas, design and tasks. Treat the realm house as the constitution. Return each finding with severity and its earliest owning artifact; zero findings is consistent.

Judge underspecified areas, unquantified language, missing decisions, capability/delta mismatches, and requirements without adequate scenarios. Return every ambiguity with the evidence needed to settle it; zero findings is clear.
instructions.design:
# OpenSpec design

Write `openspec/changes/<change>/design.md`. Record context, goals and non-goals, decisions with alternatives, risks, migration, and open questions. On return, revise the design and dependent artifacts so no finding is merely acknowledged.

Revise the returned change in dependency order. Encode an answered ambiguity as a scenario, record design choices under `## Decisions`, and keep every dependent artifact coherent. Record a reasoned refusal in the owning artifact.

wrote which capability, so every capability the change touched carries a
`## Provenance` list.

After the archive operation, open each capability's
`openspec/specs/<capability>/spec.md` that the change touched and append
exactly one line under a `## Provenance` heading held at the end of the
file:

`- \`<archived-directory-name>\` — folded <YYYY-MM-DD>`

`<archived-directory-name>` is the directory the archive operation
created under `openspec/changes/archive/`; `<YYYY-MM-DD>` is the day it
was folded. Append only: never rewrite, reorder or remove an existing
provenance line, because standing truth accumulates and is not edited into
a different meaning. The line is a pointer, not a summary — it names the
change and nothing else, and the why stays in the change directory.

house.content:
This realm is a Rust workspace. Production code is Rust under `crates/`; the
Rust-only architecture is recorded by decision 0009. Semantic changes carry a
decision document with status `proposed` because only the operator accepts one.
Intake seats read `README.md` and decisions 0004 and 0005 before framing a
commission, along with the code and history it touches.

The frozen v1 contracts under `contracts/`, the production table at
`policy/phase-machine.json`, and `reference/` (its schemas included) are
read-only.
A contract change lands as a new version file beside the old one, never as an
edit. The evaluator corpus under `fixtures/` is also frozen and is never
regenerated, only versioned.

Tests are part of every change. Extend the suite that proves the code, run
`cargo test --workspace`, compile `recipes/self`, and leave formatting, clippy,
and the exact-coverage gate clean before reporting success.

Commit completed work with `git` using the repository's message style. Never
push.

The supported hosts are Linux and macOS (decision 0063); WSL2 is Linux. Write
no Windows-conditional code, test or evidence.

## Architecture

Decision 0071 rules how code here is shaped. Build to it, and cite its ruling
numbers in what you judge. Where a gate named below holds a rule, the gate is
the authority, and a finding it would catch is the gate's.

- **Pure core (ruling 1).** `brokkr-core` and `brokkr-view` do no I/O and read
  no clock, environment or randomness. They run no process. Pass `now`, paths
  and environment in as arguments. Effects live in the crates above core and
  view, and are journaled.
- **Enums and data, not traits (ruling 2).** A closed set is an enum matched
  exhaustively, with no wildcard arm that decides behaviour. Anything an
  operator extends is data under `adapters/`, `agents/`, `recipes/` or
  `realms.json`, validated and digested. Add a trait only for a seam whose
  contract spans several operations that must stay consistent with one
  another, reached across a process or service boundary, and name that seam
  in its doc comment. `ProducerTransport` is the one such trait today. A test
  double alone does not make a seam: a single substitutable function is a
  closure seam (`*_with`, `*_in`), which is how the house inverts a
  dependency otherwise.
- **Typed at the edge (ruling 3).** Parse wire, file and harness data once
  into a type, with `serde` and `deny_unknown_fields` where the contract is
  closed. `serde_json::Value` never goes past the edge, into state, or back
  out by string key. Never put `format!("{:?}")` in anything digested or
  journaled. A doubly-optional field or a string vocabulary is a missing enum.
- **Small functions (ruling 4).** New and changed functions stay within 100
  lines, nesting depth 5 and 7 parameters. Cyclomatic complexity follows
  the operator's 2026-09-26 ruling: a function may reach the higher of 15
  and its baseline, so a new function stays within 15, an existing one may
  change freely up to 15, and one already over 15 may only shrink.
  Production files stay within 800 lines and test files within 2,000, and a
  file already over may not grow. Add no new `jscpd` clone in production
  code, test code or data. `quality/` holds the measured baseline. Today's
  offenders carry `#[allow(clippy::…)]`, and #337 converts them to
  `#[expect(clippy::…, reason = "…")]`. Add a suppression only by a ruling,
  and remove it when you fix the function. A new suppression is
  `#[expect(…, reason)]`, never `#[allow]`.
- **Once (ruling 5).** Every fact has one home. A repeated vocabulary, skeleton
  or helper becomes one function or one table. An agent is defined once under
  `agents/`, and seats hire it by reference. A recipe that differs from another
  by a model, a seat or an entry is an `extends` overlay, never a copy. The
  agent library does not yet accept `extends`, and #360 builds it. Until then,
  a variation of an agent lives at the seat that hires it, overridden in a
  recipe overlay. It is never a second agent file that restates the first. A
  copy that must exist, such as a script a bundle pins, is held to its source
  by a test.
- **Nothing unused (ruling 6).** Add no alias, agent, contract version, flag or
  `pub` item without a consumer, and prefer `pub(crate)`. A deprecation names
  the release that removes it.
- **One derivation (ruling 7).** A fact shown on two surfaces is derived once
  in `brokkr-view`. The CLI, the TUI and `ui.html` only paint it. The engine
  never admits anything by a display-crate function.
- **Typed errors (ruling 8).** Return a `thiserror` enum whose `Display` keeps
  the operator's text. Tests match variants and pin each module's text once.
  Add no new `Result<_, String>`.
- **Tests that bind (ruling 9).** Assert exact values or variants, never
  `is_err()` alone. Show that every new test binds: a compiling mutation that
  removes the behaviour must make it fail. Restore the behaviour and record
  the failing test. Share fixtures through builders. Never change the process
  environment without a guard that restores it on unwind. A production guard
  left out because the exact-coverage gate would count it unreachable carries
  a removal-control test for the invariant that makes it unreachable, and the
  comment explaining the omission names that test.
- **The house's patterns (ruling 10).**
  - A harness is a module behind `AdapterKind`. This is the target form;
    today all five kinds share one module, and #347 and #348 build the
    split.
  - A CLI verb is a `Cmd` variant plus a handler.
  - A long parameter list becomes a parameter object.
  - Argv and mount tables are built with a builder.
  - Observing the world is split from deciding on it.
  - Never use a trait-object registry for a closed set.

Judges rate a finding against these rulings by this table, and cite the ruling
number:

- **info:** something a house gate would catch. The gate's verdict is the
  authority.
- **low:** a new or changed function over a ceiling, a rule written a second
  time, an item added without a consumer, or a `Value` carried past its edge
  within one module.
- **medium:** an untyped vocabulary that crosses crates, recipe or agent data
  copied instead of extended, a fact derived a second time on another surface,
  an error matched by its text, or a new test that cannot fail.
- **high or above:** any violation that hides a fail-open path or weakens a
  refusal. It is carried as a security finding.

A principle the implementer bent knowingly, and named with its reason in
`notes`, is still rated, and the judge carries that reason with the finding.

## Release configuration

The release manager prepares the candidate and profile patches; the operator
publishes them. Local validation is preparation work. Remote CI on the final PR
head, publication, channel updates and live-profile verification are handoff
steps, recorded as pending until their remote results exist. Historical
"live from" channel versions and old journal examples are historical facts,
not current-version references to replace.

result.notes: Implemented the recommended re-exec isolation for #936. One shared helper, crates/brokkr-runtime/tests/support/git.rs::in_clean_git_config, re-executes a test alone in a child with GIT_CONFIG_COUNT, every GIT_CONFIG_KEY_n/GIT_CONFIG_VALUE_n, and GIT_CONFIG_PARAMETERS removed, then asserts exactly one test ran and passed; the test process's own environment is never mutated, which is why re-exec was chosen over a guard in a parallel test binary. Hardened all 13 walk_908 tests that failed under the plant (including the existing hostile-global test, whose child had inherited the plant) and queued_launch's a_nested_folder_made_after_queueing_refuses_the_start. No production line changed; every existing test keeps its name and assertions. Reproduced before the change with GIT_CONFIG_COUNT=1 GIT_CONFIG_KEY_0=core.excludesFile GIT_CONFIG_VALUE_0=/tmp/brokkr-936/hostile-excludes (a file listing roles/): the walk_908 test and the queued_launch test failed with "seat 'review' names role 'roles/...'". After the change both pass under that plant, and the full bundle:: filter reports 420 passed / 0 failed while queued_launch reports 8 passed / 0 failed under it. Gates: cargo fmt --all -- --check; cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features --locked -- -D warnings; cargo test -p brokkr-runtime --lib --locked -- bundle:: (420 passed); cargo test -p brokkr-runtime --test queued_launch --locked (8 passed); typos --hidden; quality/ratchet.sh files; quality/ratchet.sh clones; git diff --check. Touched files are 966/586/603/101 lines (test ceiling 2,000); cargo-crap measures the new helper at CC 7 and the max across touched files at 7. Removal controls observed then restored: dropping the helper's cleaning made both named regressions fail under the plant with the quoted refusal. Commit 32c1ae898 is signed off with the Co-Authored-By trailer last, and git status --short is clean. TMPDIR was /tmp/brokkr-936/tmp, outside the worktree. Known host flakes were not hit.

cargo test --workspace: 41 successful test-suite summaries, 0 failed; cargo run -p brokkr-cli -- compile --bundle recipes/self: 1 bundle compiled, 0 failed (offline from the bound Cargo registry cache)

members.adversarial: MEDIUM: the new re-exec races queued_launch's process-wide CWD (decision 0071 ruling 9). tests/support/git.rs:33-46 spawns without setting a stable current_dir; queued_launch.rs:383-387 calls it outside the CWD mutex. Another concurrently running test can have temporarily changed the parent's directory to its Fleet; the child inherits that directory, and the parent restores its CWD and drops/removes that Fleet while the child is running. The child saved that inherited directory in Standing::was; Standing::drop then panics at queued_launch.rs:50 restoring it with set_current_dir(): ENOENT. Reproduction: create /var/tmp/brokkr-936-review in the same command, TMPDIR=/var/tmp/brokkr-936-review, write roles/ plus newline to $TMPDIR/excludes, export GIT_CONFIG_COUNT=1 GIT_CONFIG_KEY_0=core.excludesFile GIT_CONFIG_VALUE_0=$TMPDIR/excludes; repeatedly run target/debug/deps/queued_launch-a976a0cb67eeb7e7 --test-threads=8 (up to 400 times). Observed failure on iteration 1 under the plant: a_nested_folder_made_after_queueing_refuses_the_start FAILED, 7 passed / 1 failed, child Standing::drop set_current_dir() NotFound; expected 8 passed. Without the plant, the same concurrent probe also failed on iteration 62. Serial control: 100 consecutive --test-threads=1 runs passed under the identical plant. Give the spawned child a stable directory or synchronize directory capture/spawn with this binary's CWD guard; return to implementation, no fix by this seat. Both required exact regressions passed under the plant; the full planted bundle suite passed 420/420 and queued_launch passed 8/8 before stress. Reviewed all four changed files; production/frozen inputs unchanged. Read-only review; no tracked edits or commits.
members.correctness: Reviewed all changes a6c965d8b..32c1ae898 and commit evidence against #936, decisions 0063/0083 and 0071 rulings 2, 3, 5, 6, 8 and 9. No findings. Recommended shared re-exec isolates Bundle::compile and its children without mutating the parallel test process; existing names/assertions remain. No production or frozen data changes. result.notes: Chief synthesis of the panel (adversarial: residual medium; correctness: clean; glm: clean) over 32c1ae898, read-only, no tracked edit or commit. Floor: the panel reported residual, so this seat rules residual at medium. ONE SURVIVING FINDING, MEDIUM, raised by adversarial and confirmed by the chief's own read and reproduction (decision 0071 ruling 9: a test's verdict is its own; the house table's tier for a new test whose verdict is not bound to its subject). The new in_clean_git_config re-exec (tests/support/git.rs:29-50) spawns the child without a current_dir, and queued_launch.rs:384 calls it before Standing::in_dir takes the binary's CWD lock at :389. A sibling test standing in its Fleet tempdir at spawn time hands that directory to the child as its inherited cwd; the sibling then restores and drops its Fleet while the child runs, and the child panics either on entry at queued_launch.rs:42 (current_dir() NotFound) or on drop at :50 (set_current_dir(was) NotFound), which fails the parent's assertion at git.rs:49. Chief reproduction, test binary target/debug/deps/queued_launch-a976a0cb67eeb7e7 run from the worktree with TMPDIR=/tmp/brokkr-936-chief (this box keeps no /var/tmp across calls): (1) plant exported (GIT_CONFIG_COUNT=1, GIT_CONFIG_KEY_0=core.excludesFile, GIT_CONFIG_VALUE_0=<scratch file listing roles/>), --test-threads=8, loop to first failure: FAIL on iteration 69, a_nested_folder_made_after_queueing_refuses_the_start FAILED, child panicked at queued_launch.rs:50:46 Os { code: 2, kind: NotFound }, 7 passed 1 failed; expected 8 passed every run. (2) No plant, --test-threads=8: FAIL on iteration 26, same test, child panicked at queued_launch.rs:42:43 NotFound, 7 passed 1 failed; the race is independent of the plant. (3) Plant exported, --test-threads=1: 100 consecutive runs, 8 passed each. The lib binary has no set_current_dir (grep of crates/brokkr-runtime/src), so the thirteen wrapped walk_908 tests and the hostile-global re-exec are not exposed; the defect is confined to queued_launch. Return to implement, no fix by this seat: give the spawned child a stable directory in the shared helper (for instance current_dir(env!(CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR)) or a directory the parent owns for the child's lifetime), or hold the CWD lock across the spawn in queued_launch; prove it with the same parallel loop.
